Name: neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mpp
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mpp can perturb MPRV privilege mux, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at ctrl_o.lsu_priv.
Justification: MPP supplies the effective LSU privilege under MPRV, so a fault can elevate or corrupt ctrl_o.lsu_priv.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv can perturb effective-privilege selection, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at ctrl_o.lsu_priv.
Justification: MPRV selects whether data accesses use MPP, making a fault capable of switching the privilege source seen by the LSU.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.csr.prv_level
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on neorv32_cpu_control.csr.prv_level can perturb effective-privilege selection, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at ctrl_o.lsu_priv.
Justification: The architectural privilege register directly feeds effective LSU privilege, so its corruption can change access authority.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl.csr_we
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl.csr_we can perturb privilege CSR update, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at ctrl_o.lsu_priv.
Justification: A spurious or suppressed CSR write can corrupt the privilege state subsequently used to form ctrl_o.lsu_priv.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.env_exit
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on neorv32_cpu_control.env_exit can perturb privilege restoration -> csr.prv_level, producing an unintended value, enable, or transition at ctrl_o.lsu_priv.
Justification: This environment-return control triggers privilege restoration; a fault can apply the wrong privilege transition to LSU accesses.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.csr.dcsr_prv
Structural Path: csr.dcsr_prv -> debug-return privilege restoration -> csr.prv_level -> ctrl_o.lsu_priv
Attack Scenarios: During a legal DRET, a transient fault on dcsr_prv can restore machine privilege instead of user privilege, immediately changing the effective privilege used by later LSU accesses.
Justification: Although the measured escape window is rare, dcsr_prv is the direct architectural source loaded into prv_level on debug return; the narrow legal-mode condition explains the high masking without invalidating the mechanism. The measured threat evidence is weak because the legal activation window is rare, but SecID retains it for the direct privilege-transition mechanism.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl.csr_addr
Structural Path: ctrl.csr_addr -> mstatus CSR decode -> mstatus_mpp/mstatus_mprv -> ctrl_o.lsu_priv
Attack Scenarios: While a legal CSR write is active, a transient address fault can redirect that write to mstatus, corrupting MPP or MPRV and therefore the LSU effective privilege.
Justification: Restored by mechanism-led review: csr_addr is the exact selector of the privilege-bearing mstatus write case. Threat evidence is absent rather than contradictory, and the attack requires a bounded legal CSR-write window.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.csr_valid
Structural Path: csr_valid -> illegal_cmd -> instruction exception control -> CSR write suppression -> privilege CSRs -> ctrl_o.lsu_priv
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault forcing csr_valid to 111 can make an unimplemented, read-only, or privilege-disallowed CSR access appear legal, allowing a privilege-state write to proceed.
Justification: Restored because csr_valid is the explicit implemented/read-write/privilege authorization vector used by illegal_cmd. Its mechanism is a direct legality bypass, not generic control influence.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.illegal_cmd
Structural Path: illegal_cmd -> instr_il/exception buffer -> S_SYSTEM CSR-write suppression -> privilege CSRs -> ctrl_o.lsu_priv
Attack Scenarios: A transient deassertion of illegal_cmd during an unauthorized SYSTEM instruction can suppress the illegal-instruction exception and permit its CSR operation to reach privilege state.
Justification: Restored because illegal_cmd is the canonical rejection boundary whose value directly determines whether the SYSTEM operation is trapped before a CSR write.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.exec.ir
Structural Path: exec.ir -> SYSTEM/CSR decode and operand fields -> privilege CSR update -> ctrl_o.lsu_priv
Attack Scenarios: A transient instruction-register fault can change a legal instruction into a CSR write, alter its CSR address, or change the immediate/register operand bits that update MPP or MPRV.
Justification: Retained as a rare-window mechanism override: feasibility is maximal and the executed instruction directly supplies the CSR opcode, address, and operand; high masking reflects that only a small subset of instruction faults form a privilege-changing operation. The measured threat evidence is weak because the legal activation window is rare, but SecID retains it for the direct privilege-transition mechanism.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.debug_ctrl.run
Structural Path: debug_ctrl.run -> trap-exit source selection -> dcsr_prv/mstatus_mpp -> csr.prv_level -> ctrl_o.lsu_priv
Attack Scenarios: At trap exit, a transient fault on debug_ctrl.run can select the debug-return privilege source instead of the machine-return source, restoring an unintended privilege level.
Justification: Retained because feasibility is maximal and this bit directly chooses the privilege-restoration branch at environment exit; the high masking is consistent with the narrow trap-exit activation window. The measured threat evidence is weak because the legal activation window is rare, but SecID retains it for the direct privilege-transition mechanism.
